RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Tuesday,  April 27, 2010/V aisakha 7, 1932 (Saka)
————
(Ministries : Civil Aviation; Finance; Health and Family Welfare; Heavy
Industries and Public Enterprises; Panchayati Raj; Petroleum and
Natural Gas; Rural Development; Shipping)
Total number of questions — 20
Check on illegal medical practice in
the country
*441. SHRI NAND KUMAR SAI: Will
the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the issue of illegal medical
practice by fake  doctors/quacks in the
country has been discussed by the National
Human Rights Commission in the recent
past;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the names of various organisations
which participated in the discussion;
(d) the details of measures suggested
by various organisations to check the illegal
medical practice in the country; and
(e) the details of steps taken by
Government, so far, in this regard?
Legislation to end discrimination
against HIV/AIDS citizens
*442. DR. E.M. SUDARSANA
NATCHIAPPAN: Wi ll the Minister of
HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government proposes to
bring a legislation to save the HIV/AIDS
affected citizens from discrimination; and
(b) if so, by when will this legislation
be brought?
Review of NRHM
†*443. SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD: Will the Minister of HEALTH
AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the review of
National Rural Health Mission (NRHM)
is carried out every year by a Common
Review Mission;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it has been mentioned in
the report of the Common Review Mission
that the use of costly branded medicines,
in place of cheap generic medicines, is being
imposed in rural areas; and
(d) if so, the details thereof and the
reaction of Government thereto?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
135

136
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Legislation to check siphoning off of
black money
*444. PROF. P . J. KURIEN: Will the
Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:
(a) the details of efforts being made by
Government to bring back the vast sums of
black money siphoned off from the country
and deposited in the banks in tax havens
abroad;
(b) whether Government is
contemplating to modify and strengthen
the existing laws, or to bring any new
comprehensive legislation to check  such
siphoning off of black money from the
country; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Commission to doctors on prescribing
medicines
†*445. SHRI BHAGWATI SINGH:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that doctors get
upto fifty per cent flat commission on
prescribing several medicines;
(b) if so, whether Government is taking
any measure to control this practice of
payment of commission to doctors in the
health sector; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Incidence  of  anaemia  and
malnourishment among
young mothers
*446. SHRI MOHD. ALI KHAN: Will
the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether there is a high incidence of
anaemia and malnourishment among young
mothers with little or no access to child
planning, especially in the rural areas of
our country as compared to urban areas;
(b) if so, the comparative details thereof
in each State in the Eleventh Five Year Plan;
and
(c) the funds allocated and spent in this
regard in Andhra Pradesh, compared to
other States for the period, urban and rural
area-wise?
Free healthcare for senior citizens
*447. SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI: Will the Minister of HEALTH
AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government has any plan
to formulate a healthcare policy providing
free healthcare to senior citizens in hospitals
in view of the fact that they face great
hardships in getting treatment;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Revision of price of natural gas
*448. DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government proposes to
hike the natural gas prices produced by
State-run Oil and Natural Gas Corporation
(ONGC) and Oil India Ltd. (OIL) by as
much as 30 per cent;
(b) if so, whether his Ministry has
circulated a Cabinet Note for the move
under the Administered Price Mechanism
(APM); and
(c) if so, by what time a final decision in
this regard is likely to be taken?

137
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Special tax on indigenously produced
oil and gas
*449. SHRI P. RAJEEVE: W ill the
Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:
(a) whether any special tax is imposed
on crude oil explored and produced in the
country which is same as the customs duty
on imported crude oil;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) how the introduction of 5 per cent
customs duty has been reflected in the price
of petrol and diesel in the retail outlets?
Allocation of gas at APM rates
*450. SHRI KANJIBHAI PA TEL: Will
the Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that in Delhi and
Mumbai natural gas is allocated at
Administered Price Mechanism (APM)
rates for providing Compressed Natural
Gas (CNG) in the transportation sector;
(b) whether the State Government of
Gujarat has also requested the Central
Government for allocation of natural gas at
APM for transportation sector in the State;
and
(c) if so, the reaction of Government
thereto?
Unani hospital in Kolkata
*451. SHRI AHMAD SAEED
MALIHABADI: Will the Minister of
HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has any
scheme to promote Unani Tibbia and Unani
medical education in the country,
particularly in Kolkata;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the number of Unani medical
hospitals in India, particularly in West
Bengal;
(d) whether it is a fact that Unani
Medical Hospital in Central Kolkata is in a
very deplorable condition; and
(e) the steps taken by Government to
provide infrastructure to the hospital, like
staff, medicine, equipment and furniture to
improve its overall condition?
Anti-dumping duty on steel
†*452. SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA: Will
the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government has imposed
anti-dumping duty of  2,254 dollar per tonne
on the import of cheap stainless steel being
imported from America, European Union,
China and some other countries;
(b) if so, the percentage rise in price of
steel which consumers would have to bear
as a fallout of this step of Government;
and
(c) the rationale behind this step of
Government?
Banking facility in Jharkhand
*453. MS. MABEL REBELLO: Will
the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that in most of
the Left Wing Extremism (LWE) affected
districts of Jharkhand there is just one bank
in a block;
(b) if so, by when the number of banks
would be increased in these areas to at least
a bank in each of the Panchayat
Headquarter;

138
(c) by when the total financial inclusion
of people of LWE districts would be
achieved so that the money-lenders are
given a go by altogether; and
(d) the projection of setting up bank
branches, year-wise, district-wise and
block-wise in the State?
New agency for estimating black
money
*454. SHRI D. RAJA: Will the Minister
of FINANCE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
is considering a proposal to set up a new
agency  to undertake a comprehensive
study on the quantum of black money in
the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether this agency will also study
the illegal money stashed in secret bank
accounts outside the country; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Interest rates charged
 by SHGs
*455. SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Self-
Help Groups (SHGs) are allowed to charge
any rate of interest;
(b) whether it is also a fact that these
groups charge as much as 36 per cent or
more per year from small loanees in the
rural areas; and
(c) if so, how does Government plan to
help the small loanees to get loans at much
lower rates for their survival?
Expansion of NRLM
*456. SHRI PENUMALLI MADHU:
Will the Minister of RURAL
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the aims and objectives of the
National Rural Livelihood Mission
(NRLM);
(b) whether his Ministry is planning to
expand this programme in the current year,
i.e. 2010-11; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Survey of MNREGS workers
*457. SHRIMATI KANIMOZHI: Will
the Minister of RURAL
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has undertaken
an education-wise survey of the
beneficiaries under Mahatma Gandhi
National Rural Employment Guarantee
Scheme (MNREGS);
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) if not, how does Government match
the skills of the beneficiaries with the work
requirements under MNREGS;
(d) whether Government intends to
provide training for the beneficiaries in skills
relevant to the administration and
implementation of the Scheme; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
Sale of spurious medicines in the
country
†*458. DR. PRABHA THAKUR: Will
the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the sale of substandard and
spurious medicines is continuing in the
country;
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

139
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(b) whether such drugs are jeopardizing
the health of patients;
(c) if so, the persons held responsible
by Government for such medicines;
(d) the number of cases of spurious
medicines reported during the past two
years and names of the States where
maximum volume of spurious medicines
are being produced and sold; and
(e) the action taken against the accused
in such cases?
Death of infants
†*459. SHRI BRIJ BHUSHAN
TIWARI: Will the Minister of HEALTH
AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that three lakh
infants die every year in the country in the
first minute of their birth;
(b) if so, whether any State-wise enquiry
has been conducted in this regard; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Doctors in the country
†*460. SHRI Y .P . TRIVEDI: Will the
Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) the total number of doctors in the
country;
(b) whether this number also includes
the names of doctors who have expired or
migrated;
(c) the method adopted to find out the
actual number of active doctors;
(d) whether any proposal of the Medical
Council of India (MCI) regarding renewing
the registration of doctors every five year,
is pending with Government; and
(e) if so, by when Government would
take any decision after considering the said
proposal?
N
EW DELHI; V . K. AGNIHOTRI,
The 21st April, 2010 Secretary-General.
